The Economics Of Wildfires And Heatwaves In Europe

Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 31 Jul 2026

With France and Spain racing to combat wildfires that are raging on an unprecedented scale just as another heatwave sweeps across southern Europe, it pays to ask whether climate-related events can materially affect the European macro outlook. In economic terms, both wildfires and heatwaves can be understood as negative supply shocks. Their economic effects, however, operate through different channels.Wildfires are discrete climate events that destroy physical capital and inflict severe human costs. Their impact on aggregate output, however, tends to be limited for three main reasons. First, fires are usually concentrated in both geography and time, limiting their macroeconomic significance. Second, some of the lost output can usually be recovered once the fire has been contained. Third, reconstruction spending and government support tend to stimulate activity after the shock.
